title: Correlation IDs and distributed tracing across services
hook: A correlation ID is a unique string that ties together every log, trace, and error from one user action across multiple services. When checkout fails, you search one ID and see the full story from the gateway through payment to inventory.

blocks.text: A correlation ID (also called request ID or trace ID) identifies a single logical operation across HTTP calls, message queues, and background jobs. Clients may send X-Correlation-Id or X-Request-Id headers; if absent, the API generates one. Middleware stores it in HttpContext.Items, adds it to response headers, injects it into ILogger scopes, and forwards it on outbound HttpClient calls. OpenTelemetry's trace id (W3C traceparent) serves a similar role at the tracing layer — senior systems align correlation id with trace id or map between them explicitly. Distributed tracing across microservices requires every hop to read incoming headers and propagate them downstream.

entries.plainDefinition: Business-friendly unique id linking logs and support tickets across services — often UUID or trace id string.
Standard header encoding trace-id and parent-span-id for OpenTelemetry propagation.
Built-in HttpContext.TraceIdentifier — unique per HTTP request; can be used as correlation id.
Key-value context propagated across services alongside trace context — e.g. tenant-id, user-segment.

blocks.text: Without correlation, support teams cannot connect a user's error screenshot to backend logs. Microservice debugging without propagation means five separate log searches guessing timestamps. Problem Details (RFC 7807) extensions often include correlationId so API clients display it to users. In interviews, explaining middleware that generates/propagates IDs, HttpClient forwarding, and alignment with OpenTelemetry trace id demonstrates production experience.

blocks.title: Return correlation ID to the client
blocks.body: Include X-Correlation-Id in the response header and in Problem Details JSON extensions. Users and support can quote it; you find the exact request in seconds.

sections.heading: How it works step by step

items.title: Client sends request
items.body: Optional X-Correlation-Id header; SPA can generate UUID per user action.

items.title: API gateway middleware
items.body: Reads or creates correlation id; sets HttpContext.Items; BeginScope for logs.

items.title: Downstream HttpClient call
items.body: DelegatingHandler copies correlation id and traceparent to outbound headers.

items.title: Orders and Payment services
items.body: Each service's middleware reads same id; all logs share CorrelationId field.

items.title: Error response to client
items.body: Problem Details includes correlationId extension; response header echoed back.

snippet.label: Correlation ID middleware
snippet.explanation: Prefer incoming client id for end-to-end tracing; fall back to OTel trace id or new GUID. OnStarting ensures header is set even on error responses. Register early — before exception handler inner pipeline if possible.

snippet.label: Forward correlation ID on HttpClient
snippet.explanation: DelegatingHandler runs on every outbound call from that typed client. IHttpContextAccessor bridges request scope to HttpClient. OTel handles traceparent separately — both headers should travel together.

snippet.label: Problem Details with correlationId extension
snippet.explanation: RFC 7807 extensions are the standard place for correlationId in API errors. Include both business correlation id and OTel trace id for different lookup tools.

snippet.label: Message queue propagation (background worker)
snippet.explanation: HTTP context does not exist in consumers — embed correlation id in message envelope. Same pattern for Azure Service Bus application properties or RabbitMQ headers.

blocks.title: Request correlation: Express vs ASP.NET Core
Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Generating a new correlation id on every internal service hop — breaks end-to-end search. Not forwarding on HttpClient — downstream logs have different ids. Only using HttpContext.TraceIdentifier without returning it to clients. Trusting client-supplied ids without length/format validation (log injection risk). Forgetting queue consumers — correlation stops at HTTP boundary.

blocks.text: How to prove it in production: trigger an error, copy correlationId from Problem Details, search Application Insights across all role names with that property — every log and dependency call should appear. Distributed tracing across microservices: if logs correlate but traces do not, traceparent is missing on HttpClient — fix instrumentation not correlation middleware. Align strategies: use OTel trace id as correlation id (simplest), or maintain separate business correlation id in baggage. For BFF pattern, generate correlation id at browser edge; for service mesh, Istio/Linkerd may add headers — document precedence rules.

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Saying correlation id and trace id are unrelated with no propagation strategy. Not knowing HttpClient does not forward headers automatically without a handler. Claiming GUID per microservice call is correct — that fragments the story. Unable to explain how background workers continue correlation from HTTP requests.

interviewTakeaways: Correlation ID links logs and errors across services; propagate via header, BeginScope, HttpClient handler, and message envelopes.
Tradeoff: separate business id vs OTel trace id — align explicitly; sampling may drop traces but logs should keep correlation id.
Production tip: middleware early in pipeline; DelegatingHandler on typed HttpClients; correlationId in Problem Details extensions; queue message headers.

60s: Read or generate X-Correlation-Id. Store in Items and BeginScope. Forward on HttpClient. Return in response and Problem Details. OTel traceparent for span linking. Embed in async messages. Search one id in App Insights across services.
Follow-up: how do you propagate correlation through a fire-and-forget background task?
commonPitfalls: Saying 'each service generates its own correlation id' gets you rejected — propagation must preserve the original id end-to-end.
HttpClient without DelegatingHandler — downstream service logs are unsearchable from the user's error report.
Strong answer: 'Middleware reads or creates id, scopes logs, handler forwards header, Problem Details returns to client, OTel traceparent for spans, message properties for workers.'
introducedIn: Community pattern; ASP.NET Core TraceIdentifier built-in; W3C tracecontext in .NET 5+

jsTsCorrelations.note: Node uses AsyncLocalStorage to carry requestId across async calls — equivalent to HttpContext.Items plus BeginScope in ASP.NET.
nestjs-cls provides getCorrelationId() in any service without passing parameters — mirrors IHttpContextAccessor pattern.
